question: Can continued pretraining of Qwen2.5 on 5.5T tokens of cleaned, mixed code, math and text data, followed by instruction tuning, give open code models at six sizes that match proprietary ones?
hypothesis: A balanced code/math/text mixture with high-quality filtered and synthetic data, scaled across model sizes, yields state-of-the-art open code models without losing general and math skills.
contributions: Six code models (0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B/32B) with base and instruct versions under permissive licensing
5.5T-token pretraining corpus recipe with code, text-code grounding, synthetic, math and text data
Instruction-data recipe with multilingual agents, checklist scoring and a code sandbox
State-of-the-art open results on more than 10 code benchmarks

method.summary: Qwen2.5 checkpoints are continued-pretrained on 5.2T tokens of files at 8K context, then about 300B tokens of repo-level data at 32K context (RoPE base 10,000 to 1,000,000, YaRN to 128K), then instruction-tuned in two SFT stages (tens of millions of low-quality, then millions of high-quality samples with rejection sampling, plus a small FIM share) and offline DPO with execution and LLM-judge feedback.
method.task: code language-model continued pretraining, SFT and DPO

datasets.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-Data
datasets.size: 5.5T tokens total; final mixture 5.2T tokens, 70% code 20% text 10% math
datasets.source: Public GitHub repos created before February 2024 (92 languages), PRs, commits, Jupyter, Kaggle, Common Crawl code text, CodeQwen1.5-generated synthetic code, Qwen2.5-Math corpus, Qwen2.5 text corpus
datasets.preprocessing: Rule-based filtering; coarse-to-fine fastText-level filters on Common Crawl; synthetic code kept only if executable; code removed from text data; 10-gram decontamination against HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH

datasets.name: Repo-level long-context code
datasets.preprocessing: file-level FIM extended to repo-level FIM

datasets.name: Instruction data
datasets.size: tens of millions of low-quality plus millions of high-quality samples
datasets.source: LLM-generated instructions from code snippets under 1024 tokens, McEval-Instruct, multi-agent multilingual synthesis, open-source sets
datasets.preprocessing: CodeBERT language identification (~100 languages), long-tail languages randomly dropped, samples without code mostly removed, checklist LLM scoring s = w1 s1 + ... + wn sn, AST syntax check and sandbox unit tests

datasets.name: DPO preference data
datasets.source: code execution feedback (generated tests) for self-contained snippets, LLM-as-judge for others, mixed with common data

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B/32B
models.tokenizer: Qwen2.5 vocabulary plus FIM, repo_name, file_sep tokens

models.name: DS-Coder, StarCoder2, CodeQwen1.5, CodeLlama, Codestral, Yi-Coder, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, o1

training.objective: next-token prediction plus fill-in-the-middle (PSM format with fim_prefix/suffix/middle); SFT; offline DPO

other.sft: stage 1 tens of millions low-quality diverse samples; stage 2 millions high-quality with rejection sampling; a small part FIM instruction samples from tree-sitter AST blocks
other.dpo: offline DPO on code and common data; no beta or lr given

inference.max_tokens: CrossCodeEval 50 output tokens, 8192 total, 2048 cross-file context; CrossCodeLongEval and RepoEval 256 for function completion, 50 otherwise
inference.prompting: MBPP 3-shot; MATH and GSM8K 4-shot; MMLU STEM and TheoremQA 5-shot; CRUXEval with CoT; Text-to-SQL unified template after Chang & Fosler-Lussier (2023)
inference.retrieval: BM25 cross-file context for CrossCodeEval/CrossCodeLongEval; sparse retriever (Lu et al., 2022) for RepoEval

metrics.name: win rate
metrics.definition: CodeArena: percent of items where GPT-4o scores A above B; CodeEditorBench per-category win rate averaged

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no seeds or confidence intervals; evaluation code released.

results.claim: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct scores 92.7 on HumanEval, level with GPT-4o-2024-08-06 (92.1).
results.setup: Instruct model, EvalPlus HumanEval; sampling settings not stated.

results.claim: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct scores 88.4 on HumanEval, above DS-Coder-33B-Instruct (81.1).
The 32B instruct model reaches 31.4 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench (2407-2409).
results.quote: an accuracy of 31.4%, surpassing all open-source code generation models

results.claim: The 32B instruct model gets 49.6 (full) and 27.0 (hard) on BigCodeBench-Instruct.
results.quote: 49.6% on the complete split and 27.0% on the hard split

results.claim: 32B instruct reaches Aider Pass@1 60.9 and Pass@2 73.7 on 133 Exercism Python exercises, whole edit-format.
32B instruct scores 75.2 Input-CoT and 83.4 Output-CoT on CRUXEval.
Base Qwen2.5-Coder-32B scores 65.9 HumanEval and 83.0 MBPP.
results.setup: Base model; MBPP 83.0, MBPP+ 68.2, BigCodeBench full 53.6 hard 26.4.

results.claim: Base 32B averages 63.9 across eight MultiPL-E languages.
results.setup: Base model, Python C++ Java PHP TS C# Bash JS.

results.claim: Base 32B gets 88.3 average exact match on HumanEval-FIM single-line infilling.
results.setup: Base 32B; average weighted by number of samples per language.

results.claim: In the 7B data-mix ablation, 70:20:10 code:text:math averages 55.0 against 31.3 for pure code and 48.9 for 85:10:5.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B mix ablation; benchmarks Common, BCB, MATH, GSM8K, MMLU, CEval, HellaSwag; ablation token budget not stated.

results.claim: Pure code beats 70:20:10 on the code columns of Table 3 (49.8 vs 48.3 Common, 40.3 vs 38.3 BCB) even though the text says 7:2:1 outperformed all others.

results.claim: Pure-code mix collapses GSM8K to 23.8 against 64.5 for 70:20:10.
Four stages of fastText-style hierarchical filtering of text-code data raise the 1.5B HumanEval/MBPP average from 41.6 to 46.8.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, Text-Code Grounding Data, 4 filter stages (Fig 1).
results.quote: average scores on HumanEval and MBPP increased from 41.6% to 46.8%

results.claim: 32B instruct gets the best TableBench score, 45.1.

limits: No learning rate, optimizer, batch size, steps, hardware or compute stated for pretraining or post-training.
DPO and SFT hyperparameters and sample counts are not given beyond 'tens of millions' and 'millions'.
Mix ablation lacks token budget, and its pure-code average (31.3) does not match the mean of its row (37.3); the table prints 85/15/5 against 85:10:5 in text.
Pure code scores slightly higher than 70:20:10 on code-only columns of Table 3, against the text claim.
Single-run results without seeds; decoding settings for most benchmarks not stated.
CodeArena is an internal benchmark judged by GPT-4o.
Authors' stated future work: scaling data and model size, improving reasoning.
